dedupe_keys.name: us closed landfills methane decay rates and collection potential by climate region from greenhouse gas reporting program data

description: This case study uses mandatory reports to the US Environmental Protection Agency's Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program to test how climate affects the decomposition of landfilled waste. The authors, from Innovative Waste Consulting Services, the University of Florida and the EPA Office of Research and Development, took 5 to 8 years of annual methane collection data from 114 closed landfills in 29 states, about 9 percent of the landfills that must report, and estimated each site's waste decay rate and methane collection potential. The article was published in PLoS ONE in 2021 and is free to read online under a Creative Commons Zero public domain dedication. Coverage is national. Caveats: collection data reflect gas system performance as well as generation, and only closed sites were used. The study found that the mean methane collection potential of sites with under 635 millimetres of annual rainfall was significantly lower than that of wetter sites, 49 against 73 cubic metres of methane per tonne of waste, suggesting that part of the biodegradable waste in arid landfills may not decompose for lack of moisture, which challenges standard estimation assumptions. Simulation uses: climate-specific decay parameters for landfill gas, emission and site aftercare models. Related records: the CARB landfill gas tool (model-carb-landfill-gas-tool) implements first-order decay, and the EDF landfill methane map (data-edf-landfill-methane-map) gives site emissions.
